sentiment.rationale: IBM raised its full-year free cash flow guidance to above $13.5 billion (from prior expectation of more than $13 billion) and raised its full-year operating pretax margin expansion expectation to about a point (from half a point). Revenue guidance was reaffirmed at 'at least 5 percent' constant currency growth, but management expressed increased confidence, citing strong first-half performance and accelerating Gen AI book of business. The guidance raise is organic, driven by operational momentum and productivity initiatives, not primarily attributed to FX or one-time items.

summary.revenue: $17.0 billion, up 8 percent (5 percent at constant currency).
summary.eps: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations of $2.31, up 18% year/year; Operating (Non-GAAP) diluted EPS of $2.80, up 15% year/year.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025: constant currency revenue growth of at least 5 percent; free cash flow now expected to exceed $13.5 billion (raised); operating pretax margin expected to expand by about a point (raised from half a point); software revenue growth approaching double digits; infrastructure expected to contribute about 1.5 points to IBM's revenue growth; consulting growth contribution expected to be prudently cautious. For Q3 2025, management is comfortable with consensus estimates for revenue and profitability.
summary.margin: GAAP gross profit margin 58.8%, up 200 bps year/year; Operating (Non-GAAP) gross profit margin 60.1%, up 230 bps. GAAP pre-tax income margin 15.3%, up 120 bps; Operating pre-tax margin 18.8%, up 110 bps. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps.
key_risks: Geopolitical tensions prompting some clients to move cautiously.
U.S. federal spending somewhat constrained in the first half.
Consulting revenue flat, impacted by dynamic demand environment and delayed decision-making on discretionary projects.
Transaction processing software declined 2% as clients prioritized hardware spend during z17 cycle.
Distributed infrastructure revenue down 17% due to product cycle dynamics.
Global trade dynamics requiring prudent supply chain protection.
Foregone interest income from HashiCorp acquisition as a headwind to free cash flow.
key_opportunities: Gen AI book of business now over $7.5 billion inception-to-date, accelerating quarter over quarter.
Red Hat revenue up 14%, with OpenShift revenue up over 20% and ARR at $1.7 billion.
HashiCorp integration off to a strong start, with bookings growth accelerated and pipeline 3x last year.
z17 mainframe launch with strongest ever first-quarter start; 100%+ MIPS capacity shipped.
Productivity initiatives targeting $4.5 billion in annual run rate savings by end of 2025 (raised from $3.5 billion).
Software mix now ~45% of business, with ARR growing 10%.
Consulting backlog healthy at $32 billion, up over 8% at spot rates; net new business penetration up 13% year/year.
Optimism around macro environment, with particular strength in Japan, South Asia, Middle East, and resilient Europe.
New AI product capabilities (Watsonx Orchestra, z17 with Telen two processor, Power Eleven).
Rational M&A regulation environment expected to support future acquisitions.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Arvind Krishna stated 'we once again exceeded expectations for revenue, profit and free cash flow in the quarter' and CFO Jim Kavanaugh said 'we feel very confident even more confident than 90 days ago.'
